entries.clue: Garbled notice inscribed with second digital symbol (8)

indicators.note: garbled words are jumbled, so the letters of NOTICE get rearranged
the anagram has MO written into it, so MO goes inside

blocks.note: a mo = a moment, a second

annotation.surface: A smudged notice with some computer symbol written on it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like an ordinal (second digital symbol), but it is a noun: a brief moment.
annotation.definitionFit: A smiley face typed into a text message is the classic example of a small digital symbol conveying mood.

entries.clue: Advantage securing knight's approval (6)

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so ASSET holds N

annotation.surface: A knight's approval being useful to someone.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's reads as a possessive on knight but is a link: the wordplay 'is' approval.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: giving your consent or agreement to something is giving approval, as in royal consent to a bill.

entries.clue: Writer's whereabouts unsettled with book's release (10)

indicators.note: unsettled things are stirred up, so the letters are jumbled
releasing the book lets B go out of the fodder

blocks.note: B = book, removed from the fodder

annotation.surface: A writer's location unknown as their book comes out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Book's release' reads as a publication date, but it means letting the B go.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Keith of that surname was an English novelist and columnist, author of Billy Liar.

entries.clue: Gold coin from South Africa criminal pockets (6)

indicators.note: to pocket something is to put it inside, so BENT takes ZA in

blocks.note: ZA is the international code for South Africa

annotation.surface: A crook stealing a gold coin that came from South Africa.
annotation.walkthrough: 'From South Africa' looks as though it describes where the coin came from, but 'from' only links the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: The Byzantine gold solidus was known in medieval Europe by this name, from Byzantium.

entries.clue: Fuel soldier dropped: horrible smell rising (8)

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising makes the letters read upward, so NIFF becomes FFIN

blocks.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier dropped by parachute
niff is British slang for a bad smell

annotation.surface: A soldier falls, and a nasty smell comes up from fuel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dropped' looks like an instruction to delete something, but it describes the soldier: a para is dropped from a plane.
annotation.definitionFit: The British name for kerosene, burnt in lamps and heaters.

entries.clue: Stumble over words in Pigalle on consuming litres (4)

indicators.note: SUR eats L, taking it inside

blocks.note: sur is French for on; Pigalle is a district of Paris

annotation.surface: Someone drunk in Pigalle, slurring after downing a few litres.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In Pigalle' tells you to translate the next word into French.
annotation.definitionFit: To run words together indistinctly, as a drunk does, is to stumble over them.

entries.clue: Explorer Mike presumptuous coming into shelter (8)

indicators.note: M and BOLD come into the hut, going inside it

blocks.note: Mike is M in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A cheeky explorer called Mike barging into a hut.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Explorer Mike' reads as one person's name, but Mike is just the letter M.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Alexander von Humboldt was the German naturalist who explored South America around 1800.

entries.clue: Film us leaving cat food endlessly (6)

indicators.note: US leaves PUSSY, dropping out of it
without its end, CHOW loses the W

blocks.note: the letters US are taken out
chow is food; drop the last letter

annotation.surface: We walk out on the cat food, having had enough of it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cat food' reads as one thing, but cat and food are separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Hitchcock's 1960 thriller with the shower scene.

entries.clue: Are orgasms a plus perhaps in such establishments? (7,8)

definitions.text: Are orgasms a plus perhaps in such establishments?

indicators.note: perhaps suggests another arrangement of the letters

annotation.surface: A cheeky question about what is on offer at certain establishments.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a knowing description of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the question is the nudge-nudge suspicion people have about such places offering 'extras'.

entries.clue: Article by Ringoe to organise around topic (5)

blocks.note: Ringoe is the setter, so ME

annotation.surface: The setter writing an article and trying to organise it around a subject.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter naming himself stands for ME.
annotation.definitionFit: Used as a verb, as in a themed party or bar: to give something a unifying subject.

entries.clue: Like some exercises writer needed after a chocolate bar? (9)

indicators.note: the writer comes after the chocolate bar

blocks.note: Aero is a British chocolate bar full of bubbles
a Bic is a ballpoint pen, a writer

annotation.surface: Someone needing a pen after eating a chocolate bar before a workout.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Writer' is the crossword's pen, not an author.
annotation.definitionFit: Short intense efforts like sprinting or weightlifting work the muscles without relying on oxygen.

entries.clue: Clerk to Scrooge not right to be punished (5,2)

indicators.note: not right means R is taken away

blocks.note: Bob Cratchit is Scrooge's clerk in A Christmas Carol

annotation.surface: Scrooge's clerk fearing punishment for doing something wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not right' reads as wrongdoing, but it simply removes one letter.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal British idiom: you'll get a telling-off, as in 'you'll be for it'.

entries.clue: Opera in which dog devours priest (7)

indicators.note: the dog eats ELI, taking him inside

blocks.note: Fido is the stock name for a dog
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel

annotation.surface: A gruesome opera plot in which a dog eats a priest.
annotation.walkthrough: ELI is the crossword's standard priest.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Beethoven's only opera.

entries.clue: He wrote about idiot in party spoiling votes — heavens! (10)

indicators.note: spoilt votes are messed up, so the letters are jumbled

annotation.surface: Someone exclaiming at an idiot spoiling votes in a party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Idiot' is a book title, not an insult.
annotation.definitionFit: The Russian novelist wrote The Idiot, about the saintly Prince Myshkin.

entries.clue: Original chicken sent back in famous Indian (5)

indicators.note: sent back means returned the way it came, so URHEN is read backwards

blocks.note: ur- is a prefix meaning original, as in Ur-text

annotation.surface: The first chicken being returned in an Indian restaurant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Original' is the German-derived prefix ur-, meaning earliest or primitive.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Jawaharlal, India's first prime minister.

entries.clue: Noble takes one designer drug through nose (8)

indicators.note: HORN takes the pieces into itself
the drug goes through the nose, into its middle

blocks.note: horn is slang for the nose

annotation.surface: An aristocrat snorting a designer drug.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures snorting, which is why the drug goes 'through' the nose.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: of noble birth, aristocratic.

entries.clue: Savage nomad — hard one in the north? (3)

blocks.note: 'un is one in northern English dialect

annotation.surface: A tough nomad from the north.
annotation.walkthrough: In northern English speech 'one' becomes 'un', as in 'a good 'un'.
annotation.definitionFit: Attila's people were nomadic horsemen, and their name became a byword for barbarism.

entries.clue: Super Ted owns properties Henry must leave (8)

indicators.note: Henry must leave, so H comes out of THINGS

blocks.note: H = henry, the unit of inductance; removed

annotation.surface: A wealthy man called Ted whose properties have to be given up by Henry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Super Ted' looks like the children's cartoon bear SuperTed; 'super' is short for superintendent.
annotation.definitionFit: Superintendent Ted of AC-12 is the police boss in the BBC drama Line of Duty.

entries.clue: Instrument from India shielded with lead (5)

indicators.note: India is shielded by STAR, held inside it

blocks.note: India is I in the NATO alphabet
the star is the lead in a show

annotation.surface: An instrument from India protected with lead.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lead' reads as the metal, but it is the lead role.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the long-necked Indian lute Ravi Shankar played.

entries.clue: Unforgiving Old Testament so defective? (8)

blocks.note: Ruth is a book of the Old Testament

annotation.surface: A question about whether the harsh Old Testament is flawed.
annotation.walkthrough: Ruth is also an old word for pity, which is how the answer came to mean pitiless.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: pitiless, showing no mercy.

entries.clue: Certain players from GB cavalier with rules (7)

indicators.note: being cavalier with rules means treating them carelessly, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Some British sportsmen playing fast and loose with the rules.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Players' suggests sport, but these are musicians.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: people who play one brass instrument, the kind that sounds reveille.

entries.clue: What once involved two banks in a row? (6)

definitions.text: What once involved two banks in a row?

blocks.note: not riverbanks or money banks: two tiers of oars, one above the other
not 'in a line' but engaged in rowing

annotation.surface: A riddle about two banks lined up side by side.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Once' points to an ancient vessel.
annotation.definitionFit: An ancient galley whose rowers sat in two tiers, so each stroke involved two banks of oars.

entries.clue: Love found in New Milton on such a night? (7)

definitions.note: an adjective: the clue asks for the kind of night, as in 'on a moonlit night'

indicators.note: love is found inside the letters
a new Milton is a remade one, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: love = O, a zero score in tennis

annotation.surface: Romance in the Hampshire town of New Milton on a particular night.
annotation.walkthrough: New Milton is a real town in Hampshire, so 'New' hides as part of a place name.
annotation.definitionFit: Describes a night lit by the moon, the romantic kind the surface imagines.

entries.clue: Person devout ultimately exists for prayer (6)

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of devout

annotation.surface: A pious person lives for prayer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prayer' reads as the act of praying, but it means one who prays.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword-only sense: the insect holds its forelegs as if in prayer, hence 'praying', so it is a 'prayer'.

entries.clue: Guitar maker shunned by one religious reformer (6)

indicators.note: the guitar maker is shunned by one, so I leaves

annotation.surface: A guitar maker ostracised by a single religious reformer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Guitar maker' opens the clue and looks like the definition, but it is the word to cut down; the reformer is at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Martin, who nailed his theses to a church door and began the Protestant Reformation.

entries.clue: Rising hero seen with bishop in lively dance (9)

indicators.note: 'in' places the bishop inside the dance, so REEL surrounds B
to be seen with someone is to be alongside them, so the hero is placed next to the rest

blocks.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
a lion is a brave person, a hero

annotation.surface: A hero on the rise alongside a bishop in a lively dance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rising' looks like an instruction to reverse, but it is the definition: a rising is an uprising.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a rising, as in the Easter Rising, is an armed revolt against authority.

entries.clue: Meat joint and large onion used occasionally (4)

indicators.note: only some of the onion's letters are used, every other one

blocks.note: L = large, as on clothes labels
first, third and fifth letters of onion

annotation.surface: A cut of meat with a large onion, sparingly used.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Used occasionally' reads as cooking advice but means take alternate letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the cut from either side of the backbone, sold as pork or lamb chops.

entries.clue: Key — it opens throne room from the back (5)

indicators.note: IT opens the word, going in just after its first letter
read from the back, LAV becomes VAL

blocks.note: the throne is jokey slang for the toilet, and a lav is a toilet

annotation.surface: A key that unlocks the throne room at the back of a palace.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Throne room' sounds royal but is the toilet.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym used as an adjective: a key factor is an essential one.

entries.clue: Train in Kings Cross: men expecting problem? (7,8)

indicators.note: to train something is to shape it, so the letters are reworked

annotation.surface: Commuters at King's Cross station waiting for a train with a problem.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Expecting' looks like waiting for a train, but it means pregnant. King's Cross is a major London railway station.
annotation.definitionFit: The nausea common in early pregnancy is a problem for those who are expecting.
